review_notes: "When a creature hits you with an attack, you may use your Reaction to cause one wax false-face to break. The attack still hits, but the attacker becomes impressed by your Wax until the end of your next turn" is answered by combat/ext/wax_reactions.py on the shared hit_final query, for any attack, melee or ranged: the printed sentence has no "each round", so this is answered more than once a round whenever the Wax owner still has its Reaction. The text promises no separate per-activation count and no pool of false-faces to spend, so neither is invented here (an earlier version of this note claimed both; the AUTO15r3 review flagged the claim so a later extension does not implement a restriction that does not exist). The printed words are "your next turn", the Wax owner's own next turn, and that is the clock the mark counts: it is filed as an ordinary mark lasting until the end of the marker's next turn (impressed(owner, OWNER_TURN) in combat/ext/wax_edict.py). The attacker is not that creature, and because the Sovereign is answered on the attacker's turn an attacker clock would end the mark before the Wax owner had taken a turn at all. The White Wax Edict's own sentence says "its next turn", which is the creature it just stopped, so it keeps its own holder clock; the two sentences are worded differently on purpose and must not be spelled each other's way. (An earlier version of this note quoted this sentence as "its next turn" and argued the owner's clock from the words "impressed by your Wax" instead of from the printed "your"; the AUTO15r4 review flagged the misquotation because a maintainer reading it could change the correct owner clock to the attacker's. The behaviour was and remains the owner-anchored clock; only the quotation and the reasoning were wrong.)

riders: Soft Body can pass through a gap as narrow as 1 inch only if your rigid equipment can pass too. The GM checks such gaps and equipment; the table does not represent them.
review_notes: Set Body's "While these temporary hit points remain, you reduce forced movement by 10 feet" is answered by combat/ext/wax_footing.py (set_body_footing on the shared forced_movement_reduction query), which runs only while the living_wax_form_set_body state is up and the Temporary Hit Points this form itself granted are still the creature's pool: wax_footing.set_body_pool records that grant from this talent's own TEMP_HP_GRANTED event (one integer amount, on the form's own expiry) and drops the record when the pool is spent by damage or replaced by another ability's larger pool, so unrelated Temporary Hit Points never read as the form's and a bigger pool the form never replaced is not them either. The record's expiry is read from the form's own state when it is already there and is put back on the new form's clock when that state is placed again (the typed row grants the Temporary Hit Points before it places the state, and "Duration 1 minute" restarts with every use), and a fight saved before the record existed finds the same grant in its own recorded Temporary Hit Point receipts, so an older save keeps the reduction without any Temporary Hit Points being claimed that this form did not grant. A forced_movement row cannot carry the printed reduction: that row causes a push (combat/typed_executor.py block_forced_movement moves only a subject other than its caster, and only a positive distance), which is why the row here is the deferred marker the Court of Ten Thousand Candles uses for the same printed sentence.

Soft Body's and Wick Body's remaining printed lines are the living_wax_form_soft_body and living_wax_form_wick_body states; Wick Body's melee fire damage and its 10-foot candlelight until the start of your next turn are answered by combat/ext/wax_reactions.py on the shared hit_final query.

TAL_WAX_WHITE_WAX_EDICT_OF_STILLNESS.reviewed_by: claude sw-water 2026-09-28; auto-wax 2026-10-05 (the edict refuses teleports, invisibility, shape changes and the way out)
review_notes: combat/ext/wax_edict.py answers the four printed attempts once per creature per round, each against this owner's Cultivation Save DC: a teleport through teleport_check, becoming invisible or changing shape through condition_attempt, and stepping out of the wax (the sealed threshold) through movement_attempt. A failure stops the attempt and marks the creature Impressed until the end of its next turn; a success lets it go and leaves the printed wax mark where it stood.

The engine has no separate shape-shift action, so a change of shape reaches that hook as the Polymorphed or Petrified condition it produces; a shape change from any other source is not a thing this table can currently do.

review_notes: The 1 Cultivation Point buys the heated wax, and combat/ext/wax_footing.py (after_save on the failed save, then MOVEMENT_COMMITTED) applies the printed fire damage to every step the branded creature takes until the start of its owner's next turn.
